Find the hypotenuse or a missing leg of a right triangle. This free online pythagorean theorem calculator gives you an instant answer without an account, a download or sending your entries to a server. It is designed for quick everyday use on desktop and mobile. This guide explains how to use it, the formula it applies, and a worked example you can follow with your own numbers.

## How to use the Pythagorean Theorem Calculator

Start by entering your leg a, then entering your leg b. The result updates as you type, so adjust any value and watch the answer change. If the answer is not what you expected, check the value you entered first — a missing digit or a wrong unit is the usual cause. When you want a clean slate, Reset restores the defaults.

1. Enter your leg a.
2. Enter your leg b.
3. Check the result — it updates instantly as you type.
4. Use Reset to start over with the default values.

## Formula

a² + b² = c², so c = √(a² + b²).

That is the standard formula for this calculation, and it is the same one the [Pythagorean Theorem Calculator](/pythagorean-theorem-calculator) applies to the values you enter. You can work it out by hand, but the calculator is faster when you want to try several values, and it removes the risk of a slip in the arithmetic. If the figures look wrong, check your inputs first — a misplaced decimal point is the usual culprit.
